items.transit_en: Ichon Station (Line 4, Gyeongui-Jungang Line), Exit 2, then walk 150 m. An underground walkway links the station to the museum.
closed_en: Galleries closed on the first Monday of March, June, September and December (outdoor garden stays open)
items.admission_en: Free (permanent galleries and Children's Museum). Some special exhibitions cost extra.
items.booking_note_en: No booking needed for the main galleries. The Children's Museum needs online booking, but it is closed until 14 Dec 2026. Paid special exhibitions sell tickets separately.
items.english_tour_en: Free 'Museum Highlights' tour in English: every day at 10:30 and 13:00. Meet in front of the Korean Empire gallery, Permanent Exhibition Hall 1F. The schedule can change each month.
tips_en: Open late (until 21:00) on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

Some galleries are closed for renovation from 6 Jul 2026 to 28 Jan 2027: Buddhist Paintings (Rm 203), Wood and Lacquer Crafts (Rm 204), Calligraphy and Painting (Rms 202-3, 202-4), Buddhist Sculpture (Rm 301), Metal Crafts (Rm 302) and the Sa-i: Room of Senses.
Free coat storage by the main gate; free wheelchairs and strollers in the Great Hall.
No flash, tripods, selfie sticks or gimbals in the galleries.
The outdoor exhibition area is open 07:00–22:00.
items.notes: The museum no longer has a weekly closing day (only 3 holidays + quarterly gallery closure). The English booking page still shows old COVID-era text; booking is not needed for the free galleries. Next quarterly closure: first Monday of December 2026 (7 Dec).

partial.note: Galleries closed today — the outdoor garden is open

closed_en: Permanent Exhibition Hall 1 closed 30 Sep – 21 Dec 2026 (planned). The rest of the museum stays open.
items.admission_en: Free. (The museum is inside the Gyeongbokgung area, but you do not need a palace ticket to visit the museum. If you also want to see the palace, you must buy a Gyeongbokgung ticket.)
items.booking_note_en: No booking needed for exhibitions or daily tours. The Children's Museum needs online booking (Korean only, 50 people per session, no walk-ins).
items.english_tour_en: Free English tour, no sign-up (just come to the 1F lobby information desk): Mon & Fri 10:30 and 14:30; Wed 14:30; Thu & Sun 10:30. No English tour on Tue and Sat. For foreign visitors only. No tours 24–27 Sep 2026 (Chuseok).
tips_en: Open late on Wednesdays (until 20:00) from March to October only.
Last entry is 1 hour before closing.
On weekends and public holidays you cannot go inside the buildings of the outdoor exhibition area (safety reasons).
The museum has no parking lot; use the paid Gyeongbokgung parking lot.
items.notes: The Korean visitor page also contains older-looking lines (Mar–Nov Wed & Sat to 20:00; Jun–Aug Sun & holidays to 19:00) next to the current rule (Mar–Oct Wed to 20:00). We used the rule shown first on both the Korean and English pages. The English page still has old COVID text.

tips_en: Closed on Monday 28 Sep 2026 (last Monday of the month). Next: 26 Oct 2026.
The museum is next to Gyeongbokgung Palace; museum entry is free.
No food or drinks inside; no flash, video cameras or tripods in the galleries.

items.admission_en: ₩3,000 adults (foreigners aged 19–64). Free for: ages 18 and under, 65 and over, anyone wearing hanbok (show passport/ID for age). Also free on the last Wednesday of each month (Culture Day). Combined palace pass ₩6,000 (4 palaces + Jongmyo, valid 6 months, not the Secret Garden).
items.booking_note_en: Day visits: no booking, buy tickets at the gate. Autumn night viewing (2 Sep–2 Oct 2026) needs a ticket from NOL Ticket (nol.interpark.com); foreigners can also buy same-day night tickets at the Gwanghwamun ticket office with a passport (300 per day, 2 per person).
items.english_tour_en: Free English tour Mon, Wed–Sun at 11:00, 13:30 and 15:30 (1–1.5 hours). Meet in front of the information center inside Heungnyemun Gate. No booking for groups under 10. No regular tours 24–27 Sep 2026.
tips_en: Hanbok = free entry for everyone, including foreigners. You must wear both a hanbok top (jeogori) and a hanbok skirt or trousers. A jeogori with jeans, or a T-shirt with a hanbok skirt, does not count.
Chuseok holiday 24–27 Sep 2026: free entry at all 4 palaces and Jongmyo (Changdeokgung Secret Garden not included). During Chuseok the palace is open 09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00).
The raised stone terrace (woldae) of Geunjeongjeon Hall is closed to visitors from 2 Sep to 31 Oct 2026 to protect the stone railings.
Night viewing 2 Sep–2 Oct 2026: 19:00–21:30 (last entry 20:30), closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
Unlike the new 'every Wednesday free' rule at other palaces, Gyeongbokgung is still free only on the last Wednesday of the month.

Royal guard changing ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate: 10:00 and 14:00 (about 20 min). Gate guard ceremony: 11:00 and 13:00 (about 10 min). Not held on Tuesdays or when the palace is closed. Free to watch.
items.notes: English address is our romanization of the official Korean address. Night-viewing ticket price was not stated in the press release we checked. The Korea Heritage Service plans to extend free Wednesdays to Gyeongbokgung later, but no date is set. | 2026-09-26 link check: nol.interpark.com now redirects to nol.yanolja.com (ticket seller rebrand). Night-viewing ticket page to confirm.

closed_en: Every Monday (if Monday is a public holiday, it opens and closes the next non-holiday day instead)
items.admission_en: Palace: ₩3,000 adults (foreigners aged 19–64). Free for: ages 18 and under, 65 and over, anyone wearing hanbok (show passport/ID for age). Secret Garden (Huwon) costs extra and needs a palace ticket too: ₩5,000 ages 19 and over (including 65+), ₩2,500 ages 7–18, free for 6 and under. Hanbok does not make the Secret Garden free.
items.booking_note_en: Palace: no booking. Secret Garden: timed entry with a guide, max 100 people per slot (50 online + 50 sold on site from 09:00 on the day). Online booking opens 6 days before at 10:00 and closes 1 day before. Tickets sell out very fast in Apr–May and Oct–Nov. Arrive on time; late entry and refunds are not allowed.
items.english_tour_en: Palace buildings: free English tour Tue–Sun at 10:15 and 13:15 (about 50 min), meet opposite Injeongmun Gate. Secret Garden English slots: 10:30, 11:30, 14:30, 15:30 (Mar–Nov); 10:30, 11:30, 14:30 (Dec–Feb); about 70 min.
tips_en: Hanbok = free entry for everyone, including foreigners. You must wear both a hanbok top (jeogori) and a hanbok skirt or trousers. A jeogori with jeans, or a T-shirt with a hanbok skirt, does not count.
Chuseok holiday 24–27 Sep 2026: free entry at all 4 palaces and Jongmyo (Changdeokgung Secret Garden not included).
From 7 Oct 2026 the palace is free every Wednesday (Secret Garden not included).
The Ongnyucheon area of the Secret Garden is closed for repair until further notice.
The Secret Garden meeting point is 15+ minutes' walk from the palace entrance – leave time.
Koreans cannot join foreign-language Secret Garden slots unless they come with a foreigner (max 2 Koreans).
items.notes: English address is our romanization of the official Korean address. Free-Wednesday expansion starts 7 Oct 2026 (before that: last Wednesday of the month only).

items.english_tour_en: Free English palace tour Tue–Sun at 10:45 and 13:30; starts at the main information board after Daehanmun Gate and Geumcheongyo Bridge. Seokjojeon Hall English tour 11:50 and 14:50 (Tue–Sun and holidays), on-site booking.
tips_en: Hanbok = free entry for everyone, including foreigners. You must wear both a hanbok top (jeogori) and a hanbok skirt or trousers. A jeogori with jeans, or a T-shirt with a hanbok skirt, does not count.
Chuseok holiday 24–27 Sep 2026: free entry at all 4 palaces and Jongmyo (Changdeokgung Secret Garden not included).
Open until 21:00 every day it is open – good for an evening visit.
Every Wednesday is free entry.
items.notes: English address is our romanization of the official Korean address. Seokjojeon may have limited viewing on the afternoon (13:30–16:30) of the last Wednesday of some months (event days).

items.admission_en: ₩1,000 adults (foreigners aged 19–64). Free for: ages 18 and under, 65 and over, anyone wearing hanbok (show passport/ID for age). From 7 Oct 2026, free every Wednesday.
items.booking_note_en: On Mon, Thu and Fri you can only enter at set times with a guide (no free walking). Each slot takes 200 people: 100 booked online + 100 sold on site. Online booking: from 30 days to 3 days before. Groups of 10+ must book. On Sat, Sun and holidays you can walk in freely.
items.english_tour_en: English guided entry at 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 and 16:00 on time-slot days (also offered on Sundays and Culture Day Wednesdays). About 50 minutes. For foreigners (Koreans only if with a foreigner).

Weekdays are guided-tour-only: check the English time before you go.
If a weather warning is issued, time-slot days switch to free walking and tours may be shortened.
items.notes: Conflict on the official site: the hours page says time-slot (guided-only) days are Mon, Thu, Fri and free-walking days are Sat, Sun, holidays and Culture Day Wednesdays; the guided-tour page lists Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri as time-slot days and gives guided times on Sundays too. items.name_en: MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art)
items.transit_en: Anguk Station (Line 3), Exit 1. Also Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3) Exit 4, or Gwanghwamun Station (Line 5) Exit 2.
items.admission_en: Price depends on the exhibition. All Pass ticket ₩10,000 (when 3+ paid exhibitions are on). Free on Wednesday and Saturday evenings (18:00–21:00) and on the last Wednesday of each month (Culture Day). Free for people under 24 or over 65 and undergraduate students (show ID).
items.booking_note_en: Most exhibitions: buy at the museum. 'Do Ho Suh' (27 Aug 2026–9 Feb 2027) uses timed tickets: book online, or get a same-day ticket on site for a time slot (first come, first served; weekends can have long waits).
tips_en: Go on Wednesday or Saturday after 18:00 for free entry.
Bring ID or passport if you are under 24 or over 65 to get free entry.
Free MMCA Art Shuttle runs between MMCA Gwacheon, MMCA Seoul and MMCA Deoksugung four times a day.
items.notes: No regular English guided tour was found on the official visitor page (set to null). Last entry time is not stated. The 1 Dec 2026 temporary closure is only on the Korean page. Current exhibitions (Sep 2026): This is (Not) Conceptual Art (to 11 Oct), Korea Artist Prize 2026 (to 6 Dec), Do Ho Suh (to 9 Feb 2027), and others.

items.booking_note_en: Tours can be booked on the website up to 3 days before, or apply at the 2F lobby information desk. A booked tour is cancelled if you are 5 minutes late.
items.english_tour_en: Free English tour of the Korean War Room (2F), every day: Room 1 at 10:00 and 14:00, Room 2 at 10:30 and 14:30. For foreigners (bring passport or foreign resident card); up to 2 Koreans may join with a foreigner.
tips_en: Open on Sat 3 Oct and Fri 9 Oct 2026 (public holidays).
No food, pets, flash, tripods or selfie sticks inside; no bikes or skateboards in the outdoor area.
items.notes: Official site is warmemo.or.kr (run by the War Memorial Service Korea, not .go.kr). The directions page shows subway line numbers only as icons; line numbers were added from the station names. The English booking link for tours was not checked.

items.booking_note_en: No booking for individuals. School groups of 30+ must book. Large special exhibitions may use timed tickets (check notices).
items.english_tour_en: Free English exhibition tour every Sunday, 10:00–11:30 and 14:00–15:30. Meet at the left side of the stairs to the Silla History Gallery. (Notice dated July 2025.)
tips_en: Open late (to 20:00) on Saturdays from March to October.
Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond are next to the museum.
No food inside the galleries (gum and candy count as food).
items.notes: Conflicting hours on official pages: Korean sub-page says 10:00–18:00 daily with Saturday late opening to 20:00 (Mar–Oct, from 1 Mar 2026); the Korean main page says Saturdays and holidays +1 hour; the English page says Sat/Sun/holidays to 19:00 and, elsewhere, Saturday late opening to 21:00 (Mar–Dec). Book your visit on HiKorea before you go.

If you live in Jongno, Jung, Eunpyeong, Dongdaemun, Jungnang, Dobong, Seongbuk, Gangbuk or Nowon-gu, your office is the Sejongno (Jongno) branch: 2–3F Seoul Global Center, 38 Jong-ro, Jongno-gu. Tel 02-731-1799. Near Jonggak Station (Line 1) Exit 5 or 6.
items.notes: RELOCATION: Media (Yonhap Korean Center, SBS Biz, Lawissue; 23–25 Sep 2026) report the office said on 23 Sep 2026 it will start work at a new building in the Munjeong-dong legal complex, Songpa-gu, from 19 Oct 2026, after 36 years in Mokdong. Reported: visitor parking about 25 → 60 spaces; residence counters merged on 1F; the Online Residence/Visa Center and the 1345 center move in too. I could NOT find an official notice yet on immigration.go.kr (press releases, notice board, office news board checked on 26 Sep 2026), moj.go.kr or hikorea.go.kr. No official new road-name address found. One search summary gave '문정동 493' and 'Line 8 Munjeong Station, 11 min walk' but I could not trace this to an official page, so it is not used. Address above is the CURRENT Mokdong address, valid until the move. Re-check immigration.go.kr/immigration/1611 and the notice board in early Oct 2026. Office opening hours are not listed on the office's official page, so hours are left empty. Call 1345 to check.

items.address_en: 4–5F Seoul Global Center Building, 38 Jong-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul
items.transit_en: Subway Line 1 Jonggak Station Exit 6, about 80 m.
tips_en: Run by the Seoul city government for foreign residents and students.
Help with immigration, admin, welfare, jobs and starting a business; also 1:1 business counseling and Korean and culture classes.
The Seoul Immigration Office Sejongno (Jongno) branch is in the same building, 2–3F.
items.notes: The center's own page on global.seoul.go.kr returned a system error on 26 Sep 2026 (site now branded '마이서울플러스'). Facts come from two 2026 articles on Seoul's official media hub (mediahub.seoul.go.kr), written by citizen reporters, not the center itself. Languages: staff said counseling is in Korean by default, with English, Uzbek, Chinese, Vietnamese, Filipino supported and AI translation for others. Phone not confirmed on an official page (02-2075-4180 appears on non-official sites) – left null. | 2026-09-26 link check: old center page returns 404 (site rebranded MY SEOUL+). Official page URL needs re-finding.

tips_en: Search for found items and report lost items here. It replaced the LOST112 lost-and-found site.
Reporting a lost item online needs a login (simple authentication, mobile ID or certificate). You can also report at any police station or police box.
Found items are kept for 6 months. You can get a text or email alert when a match is found.
Lost license plates must be reported in person at a police station.
An app called '경찰민원24' is on Google Play and the App Store.
items.notes: Confirmed by the National Police Agency press release (korea.kr, attached PDF '260126(0900) 경찰민원24 정식 오픈'): service started 26 Jan 2026 09:00, merging 22 police sites; the 유실물종합관리시스템 (LOST112) is one of 6 systems fully merged, and merged systems were to be shut down within H1 2026. lost112.go.kr did not respond on 26 Sep 2026. ENGLISH UI: the site has a language menu (English and ~40 others), but it is a machine-translation widget (GTranslate) on the Korean site, not a separate English version – so languages set to null. The press release does not mention foreigners; whether foreigners without Korean ID/certificates can log in is not confirmed. Phone 182 hours are shown on the site as 'weekdays 09–18'; weekend/holiday closure is implied, not stated.
